_comment: The things receipts can't tell you. Edit this by hand; it is the one file that is not generated. Lives in the private data repo, never in the public one.

household.notes: Dinners every night, plus five weekday lunches planned as their own light dishes — not dinner leftovers. Breakfast is the same sandwich almost every morning: baguette, Boursin, charcuterie, a sliced cheese and cherry tomatoes. Plan it every day and put its ingredients on the order — it is the meal they eat most and it was missing entirely until 2026-09-06.

budget.note: Raised from 100 to 150 on 2026-09-04 to cover 7 dinners plus 5 planned lunches. The separate pantry-week allowance is retired — both numbers are 150 now. Observed average across 22 orders was 85,10 €, but those weeks had no planned lunches. Ceiling, not a target.

dietary.excludedReason: IBS. No heat at all — this is a constraint, not a preference. Aromatics carry the flavour instead: gingembre, ail, oignon vert, sésame, soja, vinaigre, miso.
dietary.limitedReason: Mildly lactose intolerant. Cheese is fine. Coconut milk is not dairy and is unrestricted.
dietary.dislikedReason: Told to Claude 2026-09-14: she hates olives. A taste preference, not a health rule, but a firm one — keep them off the list and out of any dish proposed. The two recipes that used them, the Sunday roast chicken and the puttanesca, were rewritten without them rather than dropped.

cuisines.notes: Indian means mild curry, never hot. Spring rolls are made often and are a favourite. Half the dinners Asian, half European (French, Italian, Spanish) — Charlotte asked for 50/50 on 2026-09-06, having found the weeks were running about 70% Asian. The library was already half European; it was this field, previously "most", that skewed the plans.
cuisines.fallback: vegetable-forward, and vary it — the European half should not be another gratin every week. Spanish and Italian count towards it as much as French.
cuisines.varietyRule: Don't repeat a dinner within a fortnight while there are unused dishes in the library, and prefer a dish never served over one already served this month.

cooking.batchNote: One base cooked Sunday that seeds two weeknights.
cooking.equipmentNote: Told to Claude on 2026-09-06. The air fryer and the muffin tin were being ignored entirely — use them. Every recipe carries an "equipment" array and the Recipes tab filters on it. A muffin tin is twelve holes; batch breakfasts and mini quiches suit it. No microwave, slow cooker, pressure cooker or barbecue is recorded — don't assume one.

staples._comment: Auto-detected from purchase history, but pin the ones that must never be dropped.

alwaysInclude.name: Ultima croquettes pour chat stérilisé adulte poulet
alwaysInclude.note: Two cats. History shows a single 1,5 kg sac per order, which runs out.

alwaysInclude.name: Canaillou, une marque Intermarché Litière végétale agglomérante à base de bois pour animaux familiers
alwaysInclude.note: Ordered in pairs every time it appears.

alwaysInclude.name: L'Or Espresso - Capsules de café compatibles Nespresso Brésil Intensité 8
alwaysInclude.note: 3 pods a day between the two of them. Named off the receipt of 15 September 2026, the first that says which L’Or she actually buys: Brésil intensité 8, in a box of 30, not the 50 the old guess assumed. About ten days, so it is on most orders.

alwaysInclude.name: L'Or Capsules de café compatibles Nespresso Decaffeinato Intensité 6
alwaysInclude.note: The decaf half of the 3-a-day, named off the same receipt. Decaffeinato is intensité 6, not 8 — Méré sells no decaf at 8 in a usable box. Lasts longer than the Brésil; strike it off most weeks.

staples.coffeeNote: Resolved 2026-09-15. Both capsules are now exact receipt names with real prices and the guess flags are gone. The only coffee before this was one box on 2025-10-09 whose name the email truncated to “L’Or Capsules de café ...”, which is why both lines were guesses at 17,64 € for a box of 50 for nine months. Méré sells neither in a 50; both are boxes of 30.

pantry._comment: Asian staples Méré stocks, from the receipts and re-checked on the site 2026-09-14. These are the receipt names — keys into data/catalogue.json, which holds each one's product page and current pack. They are not search terms.

pantry.goneNote: Found gone on intermarche.com, 2026-09-14. The only rice noodle left is Notre Sélection's flat 3 mm; the only gyoza are three fresh Ginza packs of seven, one of them bœuf ail piment. Kikkoman is still there but only as a 150 ml carafe. Recipes that use these are Charlotte's call — the catalogue carries the alternatives.
pantry.stockFindings: 2026-09-06, from a screenshot of the app: the Légumes aisle returns exactly one leek product, Parole gourmande Blancs de poireaux in a jar at 6,23 €. No fresh poireaux. Two recipes assumed fresh leeks on a guess and were wrong. Confirmed on the site 2026-09-14, along with the rest of the gaps now listed in CLAUDE.md: no fresh parsley, thyme or rosemary, no romaine or rocket, no fresh trout fillets, no manchego. Everything the app can buy is in data/catalogue.json, read off intermarche.com in Charlotte's logged-in Chrome; a screenshot into data/seen-in-app.json is still the route from her phone.

substitutions._comment: Two different things. A recipe adaptation is decided up front and reported. An out-of-stock item at basket time stops and asks.

ingredients._comment: How adventurous to be with products. Set by Charlotte on 2026-09-06.
ingredients.note: Actively use products she has not bought before — pancetta, saffron, anchovies, capers, pine nuts, manchego, gambas, leeks, mushrooms, shallots, arborio rice. These ship as guesses with an estimated price, then get looked up on the site and recorded in data/catalogue.json; once named there, the page lists them under New to you at the real price. Anything already in the receipts should still use its exact name — the key into the pricebook and the catalogue.
ingredients.avoidReason: All carry heat. The IBS rule outranks authenticity — the recipes say where they depart from the original and why.

favourites._comment: Charlotte and her partner star dishes in the page itself, and those live in the shared artifact database under library/favourites — NOT in this repo, and not in the weekly document, so they survive the plan changing. Read them off the page if you need them; nothing here is generated from this file.
